metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign the AC-1 live integration test (init/create/claim/transition/push-fetch + second-clone readback) to a specific child in the decomposition.
evidence: AC-1: 'Verified by an opt-in live integration test that drives those verbs against a real ephemeral bucket'
Docs child: 'Delivers AC-4 (docs half) and the AC-1 operator-facing configuration.' — only the config half of AC-1 is owned
Dependency/Preflight/Auto-doctor children each name AC-2/3/4 but none names the AC-1 integration test
findings.finding: AC-1's functional verification (the opt-in live integration test driving init/create/claim/transition/push-fetch against a real bucket) is not assigned to any child in the decomposition; only its 'operator-facing configuration' is claimed by the Docs child.
scenarios: Executor implements all four children but no one writes the AC-1 live integration test, leaving the core 'S3 works as a remote' claim unverified
findings.suggested_fix: Add ownership of the AC-1 integration test to one child (e.g. Preflight enforcement or a small dedicated line), or add an explicit note that Auto-doctor's child harness covers the end-to-end verb path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign ownership of parent AC-1's opt-in live integration test (drives init/mount, create, claim, transition, push/fetch reconcile against a real ephemeral bucket and asserts a second clone reads the writes back) to a specific child, or add a child for it.

Parent child decomposition assigns only a slice: 'Docs + ADR ... Delivers AC-4 (docs half) and the AC-1 operator-facing configuration.' — i.e. the docs child covers configuration, not the runtime verb sweep nor the live test.
Child b014 is documentation-only: 'No source, schema, or test changes.' — cannot deliver a live integration test.

Child 8970 explicitly makes no AWS calls: 'no AWS calls needed — the guard fails before any network I/O'; it verifies fail-closed and the non-S3 no-op, not the positive create/claim/transition verb sweep or a second-clone readback.

Child 0289's live canary is scope-narrowed to the doctor happy path: 'exercises the happy path against a real ephemeral bucket to validate the real conditional-write/multi-bundle semantics ... and pins the git_remote_s3 v0.3.2 API surface' — none of 0289's ACs assert the init/mount/create/claim/transition verb sweep or that a second clone reads back general ticket writes.
Children 2b05 (pure-function) has no git/network tier.
findings.finding: Parent AC-1's live-integration verification is not covered by any child: no sibling's acceptance criteria deliver an opt-in live integration test that drives init/mount, create, claim, transition, AND the push/fetch reconcile path against a real ephemeral bucket and asserts a SECOND CLONE reads the writes back, with ticket data residing only in the SSE-KMS bucket.
findings.location: child b014-1526-16d0-4c3f (assigned the AC-1 slice) — gap spans the whole roster
scenarios: Completion verifier checks parent AC-1's 'second clone reads the writes back' live assertion and finds no child AC that produces it; AC-1 cannot be signed off from child deliverables.
The end-to-end s3:// happy path (create/claim/transition against a real bucket, second-clone readback) regresses and no child's test suite catches it because each child tests only its own slice.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the AC-1 live verb-sweep + second-clone-readback integration test as an explicit acceptance criterion of one child (e.g. extend child 0289's live canary scope, or add a dedicated end-to-end child), naming init/mount/create/claim/transition + second-clone readback as its oracle.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the merge strategy / conflict-resolution behavior for the non-interactive heal (e.g. merge -s ort with union or a defined tie-break), since reachability alone doesn't define conflict handling.
evidence: AC-3: 'merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock' and 'every commit/event from all divergent heads is reachable from the healed tip (no head or event discarded)'
No statement of merge strategy or behavior when two heads produce a textual/content conflict during the automated merge
findings.finding: AC-3's non-interactive merge-heal does not state how a merge CONFLICT between divergent heads is handled; it only asserts full reachability of every commit/event.
scenarios: Two divergent bundles contain conflicting edits to the same ticket file; the automated non-interactive merge hits a conflict and the heal path has no defined resolution, potentially aborting or hanging the autonomous agent
findings.suggested_fix: Note that ticket history is an append-only orphan branch so a union/no-content-conflict merge commit is expected, and specify the fallback if a conflict does arise (e.g. create a merge commit preserving both parents without content resolution).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Place the store-init require_s3_helper guard at the shared engine seam (the *_core init/mount write path or _seam) rather than only in _commands/init.py, so the MCP server and library facade inherit the fail-closed check.
evidence: 'wire that guard into src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_commands/init.py'
AC-1 names 'init/mount' as a verb the integration test drives; rebar exposes CLI, MCP, and library facades that all reach the same store-init seam
findings.finding: The fail-closed require_s3_helper guard for store init is placed inside the CLI command module _commands/init.py, while rebar's init/mount is also reachable via the library facade and the MCP server; those paths would not pass through the _commands/init.py guard and could initialize/mount an s3:// store with a missing or too-old helper, defeating the fail-closed protection.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Preflight enforcement': 'wire that guard into src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_commands/init.py so s3:// remotes fail closed'
scenarios: Library facade: a consumer calling the library init/mount function bypasses _commands/init.py and initializes an s3:// store without the helper-version check.
MCP server: an MCP init/mount tool handler reaches the store-init path without traversing the CLI command's guard, allowing a missing/old helper through.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the init-side guard from _commands/init.py into the shared init/mount core function that CLI, MCP, and library facades all call, so the check runs regardless of ingress path (matching the push-side placement in the shared _store/push.py path).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in AC-3 / the Auto-doctor child that the heal serializes against concurrent REMOTE bundle-writers via the git-remote-s3 helper's per-ref lock (acquire it, then RE-ENUMERATE bundles under it), with the repo-level lock only guarding the local worktree/merge; name both locks and their distinct roles.
evidence: Plan: 'merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle'
Plan Context names the threat: 'concurrent/legacy pushes can leave two <sha>.bundle files for one ref' and 'a client without the IfNoneMatch lock is what creates the multi-bundle state'
A repo-level lock is local to one checkout; it does not serialize against a writer on another host, so it cannot alone prevent a divergent bundle from re-appearing during the heal window
findings.finding: AC-3 / the Auto-doctor child describe the heal as serialized by a 'repo-level repair lock', but a per-checkout repo lock cannot exclude the REMOTE concurrent/legacy bundle-writer the plan names as the cause of multi-bundle; the load-bearing guard against re-introducing a divergent bundle mid-heal is the helper's per-ref S3 (IfNoneMatch) lock, which the plan does not name.
findings.location: Child decomposition -> Auto-doctor (merge-heal); Acceptance Criteria AC-3
scenarios: A second agent/host pushes to the same s3:// ref while the heal is folding heads, re-creating a multi-bundle state the local lock never saw
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the Auto-doctor responsibility to read: 'acquires the helper's per-ref S3 lock, re-enumerates bundles under it (TOCTOU guard), then merges all divergent heads under rebar's local write lock and collapses them to one bundle; a raised/None lock acquisition means another client is healing and the push simply retries later.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the git-remote-s3>=0.3.2 minimum-version pin in a cited upstream source (changelog/release/commit) confirming that release is the first to ship the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock, or adjust the pin to the release that is.
evidence: Plan pins 'the optional [s3] extra (git-remote-s3>=0.3.2)' and AC-2 fails closed when the helper is 'below the pinned minimum'.
Upstream README (retrieved) confirms per-ref locking via S3 conditional writes but does not, in retrieved text, tie the IfNoneMatch lock to a specific release number.

Prior-art context claim: 'the awslabs/git-remote-s3 remote helper ... git-bundle-per-ref + an IfNoneMatch per-ref lock' — the version at which this lock first shipped is the exact predicate AC-2 gates on.
AMBIGUOUS/absence: the plan's own text does not cite the release that introduced IfNoneMatch, and this fact is load-bearing for the fail-closed pin.
A DuckDuckGo result surfaced an unrelated 'git-remote-s3 0.1.4' Rust crate on docs.rs, showing the name/version space is ambiguous across ecosystems.
findings.finding: The load-bearing claim that git-remote-s3>=0.3.2 is the minimum version providing the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock is asserted but not grounded to an upstream source (changelog/release notes/commit). Retrieved sources confirm the helper USES S3 conditional writes for per-ref locking, but none I retrieved pin WHICH release introduced it; a search surfaced an unrelated Rust crate at 0.1.4, indicating version namespaces are easy to conflate.
scenarios: A minimum pin set too low admits a helper build lacking the IfNoneMatch lock — exactly the missing-lock client the plan says CREATES the multi-bundle corruption — defeating AC-2's fail-closed guarantee.
A pin set too high needlessly blocks a working helper.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the git-remote-s3>=0.3.2 pin to the specific upstream release/commit that first introduced the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock (cite changelog/tag/commit) so AC-2's fail-closed boundary is verified, not asserted.
evidence: Plan: 'declare the optional [s3] extra (git-remote-s3>=0.3.2)'
Plan AC-2: 'the git-remote-s3 helper is absent or below the pinned minimum ... fail closed'
Plan Context: 'an IfNoneMatch per-ref lock' and 'A client without the IfNoneMatch lock is what creates the multi-bundle state'

ABSENCE: the plan text names the lock and the pin but never grounds '0.3.2 = first release with the lock' to an upstream artifact; the s3 extra is not installed here so the boundary cannot be probed from the environment
Class: Unverified (version boundary is a load-bearing external claim not confirmed in plan text)
findings.finding: The plan pins git-remote-s3>=0.3.2 and makes AC-2's fail-closed gate depend on being 'below the pinned minimum', asserting 0.3.2 is the first release carrying the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock, but cites no upstream source (changelog/release notes/commit) for that version boundary.
findings.location: Dependency plumbing child ('git-remote-s3>=0.3.2') and AC-2 ('below the pinned minimum')
scenarios: The IfNoneMatch lock actually landed in a different version (e.g. 0.3.0 or 0.4.0); the >=0.3.2 gate then either rejects safe installs or admits unsafe ones that still create multi-bundle corruption

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (or route to a SPIKE) the specific git-remote-s3 internal API the merge-heal drives — per-ref lock acquire/release, bundle-for-ref enumeration, and raw bundle object write/delete — naming the methods and confirming they exist and are stable at the pinned version, since the live experiment only proved the remote-helper protocol surface.
evidence: Plan: 'a new non-interactive self-heal that ... merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle'
Plan Context lists what the experiment proved: 'init/create/claim/push/fetch work' and 'non-fast-forward recovery ... fires' — i.e. the remote-helper protocol, not the helper's private Python API

ABSENCE: the heal reads bundle listings, takes the helper's per-ref lock, and writes/deletes bundle objects (a Python/boto3 surface), yet the plan neither names these methods nor states the experiment verified them
Class: Partially-verified (the helper integration exists and the protocol surface is Verified, but the private API surface the heal drives is unconfirmed in the plan)
findings.finding: The Auto-doctor (merge-heal) child depends on git-remote-s3's internal Python API (enumerate a ref's bundles, acquire/release the helper's per-ref lock, write/delete raw bundle objects), a surface distinct from the git-remote-helper protocol the live experiment exercised (init/create/claim/push/fetch); the plan does not name or verify this API surface.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Auto-doctor (merge-heal)'; Context 'A live experiment (this session) proved...'
scenarios: The heal calls a helper method or attribute (per-ref lock acquire/release, bundle enumeration, direct object put/delete) that does not exist or is not stable at the pinned version, so the auto-doctor fails at runtime the first time a real multi-bundle state occurs
